0.long_answer: Mohr-Tranebjærg syndrome is an X-linked recessive neurodegenerative disorder mainly associated with a mutation in the TIMM8A gene. This gene encodes the mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase subunit Tim8 A, also known as deafness-dystonia protein 1. Tim8 A is crucial for the proper import of proteins into the mitochondria, and its defect disrupts this process, leading to the clinical features of the syndrome, including early-onset sensorineural hearing loss and progressive dystonia, among other neurological symptoms.
